clue.text: Ride up and down and shoot in retaliation

parts.note: a switch is a slender shoot or twig cut from a tree
to hit back is to retaliate

explanation.surface: Someone on a fairground ride is shot at and fires back in revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: SWITCHBACK is a British name for a roller coaster, a ride that climbs and plunges repeatedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster whose track rises and falls steeply is called by this name in Britain.

clue.text: Fish bachelor caught in Isle of Wight, say

indicators.note: the bachelor's letter is held inside the island phrase, as if trapped there
signals that the island's name is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the Isle of Wight, off England's south coast, is pronounced like the colour white
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A bachelor angler lands a fish off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells you to spell the island's name the way it sounds, like the colour. 'caught in' puts the bachelor's letter inside, and an ait is a river island, a word known mostly to crossword solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are tiny young herring and sprats eaten fried whole.

clue.text: Quaver in excitement when husband's away

indicators.note: when the husband is away he is absent, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: a thrill is a sudden feeling of excitement
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: Someone trembles with excitement while their husband is out of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a rapid wavering or warbling of the voice in singing.

clue.text: American writer coming from Heathrow set out about noon

indicators.note: the scrambled airport letters go around the letter for noon
letters set out afresh are laid out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An American author arrives from Heathrow airport and leaves around midday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges HEATHROW into HAWTHORE, and 'about' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Hawthorne, author of The Scarlet Letter, was a nineteenth-century American novelist.

clue.text: Missing starter, vegetable stuffed with soft fruit

indicators.note: the vegetable, shortened, is filled with the letter for soft
without its opening letter, the vegetable loses its first letter

parts.note: a haricot is a kind of bean
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A recipe: a vegetable with no first course, filled with soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing starter' drops the H of HARICOT, leaving ARICOT; 'stuffed with' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An apricot is a stone fruit with soft orange flesh.

clue.text: King and Ruth turned up for barbecue food

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king in chess

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Babe Ruth was the famous American baseball player

explanation.surface: A king and a woman named Ruth arrive for some grilled food.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'turned up' means read from the bottom up; Babe Ruth was a famous American baseball player.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat chunks grilled on a skewer are a classic dish cooked on a barbecue.

clue.text: Guarded, using two sound characters from secret police

indicators.note: the pair of letters is to be spoken aloud as their names

parts.note: K and G are the first two letters of KGB, the Soviet secret police

explanation.surface: Someone stays careful when quoting a couple of letters from a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the letters K and G aloud, 'kay-gee', and you hear the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cagey means being cautious and secretive, keeping one's guard up.

clue.text: Criminals, we hear, had limit

parts.note: cons are convicts, criminals

indicators.note: signals that the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: to have someone is to trick or fool them

explanation.surface: Lawbreakers, we are told, had a ceiling put on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns the word for 'had' (fooled) into its sound, which is written with no -ED ending.
explanation.definitionFit: To constrict is to squeeze tighter or restrict.

clue.text: Keep silent about extremely unmerciful prison system

indicators.note: the word for silencing goes round the outer letters

parts.note: to gag someone is to keep them silent

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a merciless network of prisons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes U and L, the first and last letters of 'unmerciful'; 'about' puts GAG around them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet network of forced-labour camps was known by this acronym.

clue.text: Struggle launched on one's own?

parts.note: read as a fight started against one's own people, a conflict between citizens of one country

explanation.surface: A fight someone begins alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A war fought between groups of citizens within one country.

clue.text: Black tribesman's personal ornament

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
the Angles were a Germanic tribe that settled England

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned tribesman wears his own jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bangle is a rigid bracelet worn as jewellery.

clue.text: Arab peasant was killed by a' horse

parts.note: fell means died in battle
taken as the letter A
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A peasant died after being kicked by a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: In Egypt and Arab lands, a fellah is a farm labourer or peasant.

clue.text: Family of explorers with a lot of time for coastal trade

parts.note: John and Sebastian Cabot were father-and-son explorers

indicators.note: most of the word, with its final letter cut off

parts.note: ages is a long time

explanation.surface: A dynasty of explorers spent a long time on the coast trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabotage is shipping trade between ports along one country's coast.

clue.text: Fastener, with luck, going over front of staple

indicators.note: the word for luck covers, so sits around, the other letter

parts.note: hap is an old word for luck or chance

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: With luck, a staple's front will hold something fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' gives S from 'staple'; 'going over' puts HAP around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hasp is a hinged metal clasp secured by a padlock.

clue.text: Expert on language of birds

definitions.meaning: Eric ... was a lexicographer famous for dictionaries of slang
game birds, the plural being the same as the singular

explanation.surface: A linguist who understands what birds say.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Partridge compiled noted slang dictionaries; the game bird's plural can be unchanged.

clue.text: Dog said to become bad and get even worse

indicators.note: signals that the word is taken by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.words: become bad and get even worse
parts.note: rot means become bad, and viler means even worse

explanation.surface: A hound reputed to go bad and then worse still.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' plus 'viler', spoken the German way, sounds like the breed name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rottweiler is a powerful German breed of guard dog.

clue.text: Ring fan wearing strange article

indicators.note: something strange is odd or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A ring enthusiast sporting an odd item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring fan' looks like someone fond of jewellery; here it means a fan of Wagner's Ring operas. 'strange' rearranges 'wearing'.
explanation.definitionFit: A devotee of Wagner, whose Ring cycle is four operas.

clue.text: Fortitude of French in Alpine river

parts.note: en is French for in
the Durance flows from the French Alps to the Rhône

explanation.surface: The courage of French people living by an Alpine river.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the strength to bear hardship, a kind of fortitude.

clue.text: Valet rings with new order for tailor

indicators.note: a new order of letters means a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A valet calls up with a fresh order for the tailor.
explanation.walkthrough: Starveling is the tailor among the rustics in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Starveling is the tailor in Shakespeare's comedy.

clue.text: Popular taste I'd found bland

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a sip is a small taste of drink
the contraction of I had, written ID

explanation.surface: Something popular tasted dull to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food or company lacks flavour or interest.

clue.text: Flap requiring attention

definitions.meaning: a flap is a state of agitated fuss
still on the list of tasks to be done

explanation.surface: A panic over something that needs seeing to.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or commotion is called this, and tasks still outstanding sit on this list.

clue.text: Save joints of meat for military quarters

parts.note: save and bar both mean except
a rack is a joint of lamb or pork ribs

explanation.surface: Keep meat joints for the soldiers' quarters.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing soldiers.

clue.text: A short hearing in the courts

indicators.note: short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a trial is a hearing in court

explanation.surface: A brief hearing takes place in the law courts.
explanation.definitionFit: Atria are open central courtyards of Roman houses.

clue.text: Substitute for chocolate bar company briefly put out

indicators.note: letters put out of place are disordered and rearranged

parts.note: CO is the short form of company

explanation.surface: A chocolate substitute that a bar company has briefly launched.
explanation.definitionFit: Carob pods are ground into a powder used in place of cocoa.

clue.text: Great Power's political representative in Ireland

indicators.note: the representative is placed inside the country name

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A great power's politician serving in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An empire is a vast state ruling many lands, a great power.

clue.text: School organisation importing Italian bread

indicators.note: the school body brings in, so contains, the Italian abbreviation

parts.note: a PTA is a parent-teacher association
IT is short for Italian, as in Italian vermouth

explanation.surface: A parents' group at a school brings in Italian bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, hollow Mediterranean bread.

clue.text: Merchantman about to move suddenly astern

indicators.note: going astern means going backwards, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to dart is to move suddenly

explanation.surface: A merchant ship is about to shoot backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astern' reverses RE + DART as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant ship carrying goods is called a trader.

clue.text: Very eager to secure one old master, say

indicators.note: the eager word holds, so contains, the numeral

parts.note: panting for something means longing for it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone desperate to get hold of a work by an old master.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Master work is an example of a fine-art picture.

clue.text: Good drink, but it gives you a lot of wind

parts.note: ale is beer

explanation.surface: A good beer, though it brings on flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind.

clue.text: Been bad, and resorted to here for .. cure?

indicators.note: re-sorted means sorted again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Having behaved badly, someone goes to this place for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resorted' (re-sorted) rearranges BEEN BAD AND; Baden-Baden is a German spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: Baden-Baden is a German spa town visited to take the waters.
